description: Remove dead code from the fastai package: unused functions, unused variables, commented-out code, unused imports, and an empty module file.

In fastai/core.py: Remove the `load2` function (line 113) - defined but never called anywhere.
In fastai/core.py: Remove the `load_array` function (line 115) - defined but never called from within the package.
In fastai/core.py: Remove the `partition_by_cores` function (lines 80-81) - defined but never called anywhere.
In fastai/core.py: Remove the `SimpleNet` class (lines 97-107) - defined but never instantiated anywhere in the codebase.

In fastai/plots.py: Remove the `plots_raw` function (lines 66-72) - defined but never called anywhere.
In fastai/plots.py: Remove the `load_img_id` function (line 74) - defined but never called anywhere.
In fastai/adaptive_softmax.py: Remove unused `from math import sqrt` import (line 2) - sqrt is never used in the file.
In fastai/io.py: Remove unused `import gzip` (line 4) - gzip is never used in the file.
Delete fastai/rnn_train.py entirely - the file only contains imports and has no definitions. It is never imported from anywhere.
Verify all modified files parse correctly with: python -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('fastai/<file>.py').read())"
acceptance_criteria: All modified Python files parse without syntax errors
No functions/variables/imports that were actually used elsewhere are removed
The commented-out code block in text.py is removed
The empty rnn_train.py file is deleted
All remaining code in modified files maintains proper structure (no dangling references, proper line spacing)
verification: Run: python -c "import ast, glob; [ast.parse(open(f).read()) for f in glob.glob('fastai/*.py')]" to confirm all files parse correctly

findings: Pre-existing syntax error in core.py: 'async=True' is invalid in Python 3.7+. All available Python versions (3.10+) fail to parse core.py due to this pre-existing issue. Verified by stashing changes and confirming the same parse error on the base state. All other modified files parse cleanly with AST validation.
